messages:
Priya Rao: Heads up — seeing periodic tail-latency spikes from eu-west1-rack7 since 2026-03-15 07:20 UTC. Graphs show ~200–500ms spikes every ~2m. Correlates with GPU powercap oscillations and ambient sensor jumps. @oncall

infra-bot: [ALERT] rack7: GPU powercap fluctuation detected (threshold exceeded). Autoscaler: routing fallback engaged.

Sam Chen: On it. Can you paste node IDs and a short `nvidia-smi` / `dmesg` snippet?

Priya Rao: nodes: node-gw7-02, node-gw7-05, node-gw7-11
nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
GPU  PowerDraw  PowerCap  FanTemp  Perf
0    210W       200W      62C      P0
0    180W       250W      59C      P0
0    220W       200W      64C      P2
```
noticed `PowerCap` jumping between 200W and 250W in consecutive samples; fan RPMs oscillating.

Marc Alston: Any scheduled power-profile changes or infra jobs? Ambient sensor spikes could be PSU temp hysteresis triggering powercap. Also check for Xid/ECC in kernel logs.

Lucia Gomez: If we confirm instability, recommend draining affected GPUs, open vendor ticket for ambient sensor & PSU review. I can coordinate rolling drains.

Sam Chen: pulling logs now — `journalctl -u nvidia-driver | grep -i xid | tail -n 10`:
```
Mar 15 07:21:12 node-gw7-02 nvidia-driver: Xid (31): GPU crash
Mar 15 07:21:14 node-gw7-02 kernel: ECC error on GPU0
Mar 15 07:22:30 node-gw7-02 nvidia-driver: Power cap changed to 250W
Mar 15 07:23:58 node-gw7-02 nvidia-driver: Power cap changed to 200W
```
Draining node-gw7-02 now. Will reroute inference traffic to dedicated pool. :white_check_mark:

Priya Rao: Thanks — fallback routing kept endpoints up. Marking as P1 until vendor confirms sensor calibration and we rule out firmware regression. Posting ticket in vendors/infra with logs.
